node_labels.p2: Cold rolling of the as-cast alloy to 80 % reduction
node_labels.s1: fcc and bcc phases are both present in as-cast, cold-rolled and annealed states
node_labels.o1: Reflections marked as fcc (about 44, 51, 75, 91, 96 deg) with one bcc reflection near 45 deg
node_labels.o2: Main fcc reflection (~44 deg) intensity varies non-monotonically with annealing time, highest at 2 h
node_labels.o16: A separate bcc reflection is marked only on the 16 h annealed trace, not on shorter anneals

node_labels.s7: Mean grain size coarsens with annealing time, about 4.5 to 39 um, roughly linear in t^1/3
node_labels.o8: Measured average grain size rises with t^1/3 from about 4.5 to 39.4 um (third point 8.0 below second 8.8)
node_labels.o9: Measured grain sizes coincide with modified Z-S model points up to t^1/3 = 19.3, but the last point is 39.4 vs 30 um predicted
node_labels.o13: F4 time axis t^1/3 = 13.9-24.3 s^1/3 corresponds to about 45 min-4 h, not the 75 min-16 h anneals
node_labels.o14: F5 grain sizes (d = 30.0, 21.6, 19.2, 9.0, 7.0, 5.3 um) equal the F4 model series, not the measured sizes

node_labels.p4: Hardness falls as grains coarsen, linear in d^-1/2 (Hall-Petch), about 294 HV to 211 HV
node_labels.p5: Hall-Petch coefficient k_HV = 336.28 HV um^1/2, with intrinsic hardness HV0 = 145.94 HV
node_labels.o11: Microhardness rises linearly with d^-1/2 from about 211 HV (0.18 um^-1/2) to 294 HV (0.43 um^-1/2)
node_labels.o14: F5 grain sizes (d = 30.0, 21.6, 19.2, 9.0, 7.0, 5.3 um) equal the F4 model series, not the measured sizes

node_labels.s2: Cold rolling elongates the dendrites along the rolling direction and breaks up the dendritic morphology
node_labels.o3: Grey dendrite cores (DC) and dark interdendritic (ID) pockets are elongated along the marked rolling direction
node_labels.o4: ID pockets show a periodic fine lamellar, basket-weave pattern of alternating contrast

p2.F1.why: PARTIAL: The key states the panel shows "Cold rolling of the as-cast alloy to 80% reduction." The candidate's description does include this feature (the "Cold-rolling-80%" red curve in panel a, compared against "As-cast"), which agrees with the key. However, the candidate treats the image as containing two panels (a and b) and spends roughly half the answer describing panel b (a six-curve time-series of 75 min to 16 h), which is unrelated to the key's stated content and not confirmed to be part of the same evidence node. This dilutes/conflates the match rather than contradicting it, so it does not fully align with the key's specific, narrower claim — hence PARTIAL rather than CORRECT or WRONG.

However, for the "as-cast" curve, the candidate describes only fcc peaks (plus an unlabeled "weaker peak near 96°") without clearly identifying a bcc peak there, leaving the key's specific claim that both phases are present in the as-cast state unconfirmed/ambiguous rather than outright contradicted — hence PARTIAL rather than CORRECT or WRONG.

The only difference is terminology (candidate calls the features "second-phase particles/intermetallic/eutectic features" rather than "dendrites"), but the described visual phenomenon (elongation + breakup along rolling direction) is the same, so per the grading note this counts as agreement, not contradiction.
